nfl_afd_general.q: After a penalty for a foul by Team B prior to, during, or after a play from scrimmage, the ensuing down is first-and-10 for Team A.

nfl_afd_exceptions.q: For the above exceptions, the number of the down and the line to gain remain the same unless a distance penalty places the ball on or in advance of the line to gain

nfl_runoff.q: A team is not permitted to conserve time after the two-minute warning of either half by committing any of these acts: (a) a foul by either team that stops the clock during any dead ball period; (b) intentional grounding; (c) an illegal forward pass; (d) throwing a backward pass out of bounds;

nfl_runoff_defense.q: Item 2. Actions by the Defense. If the action is by the defense, the play clock will be reset to 40 seconds

nfl_other_personal.q: Fouls that include a 15-yard penalty but are not listed in this Section or in Section 3 are considered personal fouls for penalty enforcement purposes.

ncaa_runoff.q: before a change of team possession if either team commits a foul that causes the clock to stop immediately and the penalty for that foul is accepted, the referee will subtract 10 seconds from the game clock

ncaa_runoff_list.q: Any foul that prevents the snap (e.g., false start, encroachment, defensive offside by contact in the neutral zone, etc.) (A.R. 3-4-4-III); 2. Intentional grounding to stop the clock; 3. Incomplete illegal forward pass; 4. Backward pass thrown out of bounds to stop the clock;

ncaa_runoff_not.q: The 10-second rule does not apply if the game clock is not running when the foul occurs or if the foul does not cause the game clock to stop immediately (e.g., illegal formation).

ncaa_personal.q: All fouls in this section (unless noted) and any other acts of unnecessary roughness are personal fouls.

ncaa_personal_penalty.q: Except as otherwise noted, the penalties for all personal fouls are as follows: PENALTY—Personal foul. 15 yards. For dead-ball fouls, 15 yards from the succeeding spot. Automatic first down for fouls by Team B if not in conflict with other rules.

ncaa_flagrant.q: all flagrant fouls (Rule 2-10-3) require ejection or disqualification.

ncaa_targeting_penalty.q: PENALTY—[ARTICLE 3 and ARTICLE 4]—15 yards. For dead-ball fouls, 15 yards from the succeeding spot. Automatic first down for fouls by Team B if not in conflict with other rules.

ncaa_targeting_dq.q: for a player’s first targeting foul in a season, disqualification for the remainder of the game with no carryover disqualification

ncaa_unsportsmanlike_afd.q: Automatic first down for live-ball and dead-ball fouls by Team B if not in conflict with other rules. Flagrant offenders, if players or substitutes, shall be ejected [S47].

nfl_dead_ball_taunt.q: A dead ball foul is a foul that occurs in the continuing action after a down ends, or a taunting foul that occurs at any time.

nfl_post_possession_exc.q: Except for fouls that are committed in an attempt to block the kick (such as running into or roughing the kicker, defensive holding (pull-and-shoot), leverage, leaping, and pushing teammate(s) into the offensive formation)

ncaa_postscrimmage.q: Postscrimmage kick enforcement applies only to fouls by Team B during a scrimmage kick and only under the following conditions:

entries.name: False start

pro.q: Penalty: For a false start: Loss of five yards from the line of scrimmage. The penalty is enforced prior to the snap.

college.q: No Team A player may commit a false start (Rule 7-1-2-b) or contact an opponent (A.R. 7-1-3-III). PENALTY—[a-d] Dead-ball foul: Five yards from the succeeding spot.

entries.name: Encroachment (defensive contact before the snap)

pro.q: Penalty: For encroachment: Loss of five yards from the line of scrimmage. The penalty is enforced prior to the snap.

college.q: PENALTY [1-3]—Dead-ball foul, offside. Five yards from the succeeding spot [S18].
college.note: College has no foul named encroachment for the defense; contact before the snap is a dead-ball offside under 7-1-5-a-1.

entries.name: Neutral zone infraction

pro.q: Penalty: For a neutral zone infraction: Loss of five yards from line of scrimmage. Penalty is enforced prior to snap.

college.q: PENALTY [1-3]—Dead-ball foul, offside. Five yards from the succeeding spot [S18].
college.note: College: entering the neutral zone and causing an offensive lineman to react is a dead-ball offside under 7-1-5-a-2.

entries.name: Offside at the snap

pro.q: Penalty: For offside: Loss of five yards.

college.q: 2. All players must be inbounds. PENALTY—Live-ball foul. Five yards from the previous spot [S18].

entries.name: Illegal shift

pro.q: Penalty: For an illegal shift: Loss of five yards.

college.q: PENALTY [a-c]—Live-ball foul: Five yards from the previous spot

entries.name: Illegal motion

pro.q: Penalty: For a player illegally in motion at the snap: Loss of five yards.

college.q: PENALTY [a-c]—Live-ball foul: Five yards from the previous spot

entries.name: Illegal formation (offense)

pro.q: Penalty: For illegal formation by the offense: Loss of five yards.

college.q: PENALTY [a-c]—Live-ball foul: Five yards from the previous spot

entries.name: Illegal snap

pro.q: Penalty: For illegally snapping the ball: Loss of five yards from the line of scrimmage.
pro.note: The pro penalty statement does not say whether the ball is dead; the field is false until a second source settles it.

college.q: No player shall put the ball in play before it is ready for play (Rule 4-1-4 and A.R. 4-1-4-I and II). PENALTY [a-b]—Dead-ball foul. Five yards from the succeeding spot

entries.name: Snap to an ineligible receiver of the snap

pro.q: Penalty: For snapping the ball to a player who is ineligible to receive the snap: Loss of five yards from the line of scrimmage. The whistle shall be blown immediately.

college.q: ARTICLE 3. No offensive lineman may receive a hand-to-hand snap. PENALTY—Live-ball foul. Five yards from the previous spot [S19].

entries.name: Delay of game

pro.q: Penalty: For delay of the game: Loss of five yards: (a) from the succeeding spot if it occurs between downs and the ball remains dead; or (b) from the previous spot if the ball was in play.
pro.note: Dead-ball field true: part (b), a delay with the ball in play, is the rare case.

college.q: Action clearly designed to delay the officials from making the ball ready for play (A.R. 3-4-2-II). PENALTY—Dead-ball foul. Five yards from the succeeding spot [S7 and S21].
college.note: Runoff reading: an expired play clock is a foul that prevents the snap (3-4-4-a-1).

entries.name: More than 11 players in the formation or huddle

pro.q: Penalty: For more than 11 players in the formation prior to the snap or free kick: Loss of five yards from the succeeding spot.

college.q: Officials shall stop the action whether or not the ball has been snapped. PENALTY—Dead-ball foul. Five yards from the succeeding spot. [S22]
college.note: College 3-5-3-a binds Team A only; a Team B surplus at the snap is too_many_on_field.

entries.name: More than 11 players on the field at the snap

pro.q: Penalty: For more than 11 players on the field of play or the end zone while the ball is in play: Loss of five yards from the previous spot.

college.q: The infraction is treated as a live-ball foul (A.R. 3-5-3-I-VII). PENALTY—Live-ball foul. Five yards at the previous spot. [S22]

entries.name: Illegal forward pass from beyond the line

pro.q: (a) For a forward pass from beyond the line: Loss of down and five yards from the spot where the ball is released.

college.q: PENALTY [a-e]—Five yards from the spot of the foul; also loss of down if by Team A before team possession changes during a scrimmage down

entries.name: Illegal touching of a forward pass by an ineligible

pro.q: Penalty: For illegal touching of a forward pass: Loss of five yards at the previous spot.

college.q: touch a legal forward pass until it has touched an opponent or an official (A.R. 5-2-3-I and A.R. 7-3-11-I-II). PENALTY—Five yards from the previous spot, loss of down [S16 and S9].

entries.name: Illegal touching of a forward pass after going out of bounds

pro.q: Penalty: For illegal touching of a forward pass after being out of bounds: Loss of down at the previous spot.

college.q: returning inbounds, it is an incomplete pass (Rule 7-3-7) and not a foul for illegal touching. PENALTY—Loss of down at the previous spot [S16 and S9].

entries.name: Intentional grounding

pro.q: Penalty: For intentional grounding: (a) Loss of down and 10 yards from the previous spot; or
pro.note: The spot-of-pass alternative and the safety from the end zone are in foul.grounding.enforcement.

college.q: PENALTY [f-h]—Loss of down at the spot of the foul [S36 and S9].

entries.name: Ineligible receiver downfield on a pass

pro.q: Penalty: For ineligible offensive player downfield: Loss of five yards from the previous spot.
pro.note: The older key foul.ineligible_downfield.yards holds the downfield limit, not this penalty.

college.q: the ball away and the ball lands near or beyond the sideline.) (A.R. 7-3-10-I and -III). PENALTY—Five yards from the previous spot [S37].

entries.name: Illegal contact with a receiver

pro.q: Penalty: For illegal contact by the defense: Loss of five yards and automatic first down.

college.absent: Article 8 is headed "Illegal Contact and Pass Interference" but its penalties are those of offensive and defensive pass interference; the rule book has no separate five-yard illegal contact foul (Appendix G lists none).

entries.name: Defensive holding

pro.q: Penalty: For defensive holding: Loss of five yards and an automatic first down.

college.q: Continuous contact is illegal (A.R. 9-3-4-I). PENALTY [c-e]—10 yards plus automatic first down if the first down is not in conflict with other rules

entries.name: Defensive pass interference

pro.q: Penalty: For pass interference by the defense: First down for the offensive team at the spot of the foul.
pro.note: Spot foul: the yards field is 0 and the cap (none at pro) is foul.dpi.max_yards.

college.q: PENALTY—Team A’s ball at the spot of the foul, first down, if the foul occurs fewer than 15 yards beyond the previous spot.
college.note: Spot foul up to 15 yards: the yards field is 0 and the cap is foul.dpi.max_yards.

entries.name: Offensive pass interference

pro.q: Penalty: For pass interference by the offense: Loss of 10 yards from the previous spot.

college.q: PENALTY—10 yards from the previous spot [S33]. c. Defensive pass interference is contact

entries.name: Backward pass thrown out of bounds to save time

pro.q: Penalty: For a backward pass out of bounds before a change of possession during a play that starts after the two-minute warning. Loss of down and 5 yards.

college.q: to throw the ball intentionally out of bounds to conserve time. PENALTY—Five yards from the spot of the foul; also loss of down if by Team A

entries.name: Illegally handing the ball forward

pro.q: (a) For handing ball forward beyond the line of scrimmage: Loss of down and five yards from spot of the foul.

college.q: at least two yards behind their scrimmage line when receiving the ball (A.R. 7-1-6-I). PENALTY—Five yards from the spot of the foul; also loss of a down if by Team A

entries.name: Offensive holding

pro.q: Penalty: For holding by the offense: Loss of 10 yards.

college.q: b. Holding. The hand(s) and arm(s) shall not be used to grasp, pull, hook, clamp or encircle in any way that illegally impedes or illegally obstructs an opponent. PENALTY—10 yards

entries.name: Illegal use of hands by the offense

pro.q: Penalty: For illegal use of hands by the offense: Loss of 10 yards.

college.q: b. Holding. The hand(s) and arm(s) shall not be used to grasp, pull, hook, clamp or encircle in any way that illegally impedes or illegally obstructs an opponent. PENALTY—10 yards
college.note: The 9-3-3 penalty covers paragraphs a (use of hands) and b (holding).

entries.name: Illegal block in the back

pro.q: Penalty: For an illegal block in the back above the waist by the offense: Loss of 10 yards.

college.q: PENALTY—10 yards. Penalties for Team A fouls behind the neutral zone are enforced from the previous spot. Safety if the foul occurs behind Team A’s goal line. [S43].
college.note: Either team; the penalty carries no first down.

entries.name: Assisting the runner or interlocked interference

pro.q: Penalty: For assisting the runner, interlocking interference, or illegal use of hands, arms, or body by the offense: Loss of 10 yards.

college.q: one another in any manner while contacting an opponent. PENALTY—Five yards [S44].

entries.name: Illegal use of hands by the defense

pro.q: Penalty: For illegal use of hands by the defense: Loss of five yards and an automatic first down.

college.q: Continuous contact is illegal (A.R. 9-3-4-I). PENALTY [c-e]—10 yards plus automatic first down if the first down is not in conflict with other rules

entries.name: Clipping

pro.q: Penalty: For clipping: Loss of 15 yards.

college.q: ARTICLE 5. There shall be no clipping (Rule 2-5).

entries.name: Illegal block below the waist

pro.q: Penalty: For illegally blocking below the waist: Loss of 15 yards.

college.q: Blocking Below the Waist ARTICLE 6. a. Team A prior to a change of team possession:

entries.name: Chop block

pro.q: Penalty: For a chop block: Loss of 15 yards.

college.q: ARTICLE 10. There shall be no chop blocking (Rule 2-3-3)

entries.name: Blindside block

pro.q: Penalty: For a blindside block: Loss of 15 yards.

college.q: ARTICLE 18. No player shall deliver a blind-side block by attacking an opponent with forcible contact.

entries.name: Unnecessary roughness

pro.q: Penalty: For unnecessary roughness: Loss of 15 yards. The player may be disqualified if the action is judged by the official(s) to be flagrant. If the foul is by the defense, it is also an automatic first down.

college.q: All fouls in this section (unless noted) and any other acts of unnecessary roughness are personal fouls.

entries.name: Contact against a defenseless player

pro.q: Penalty: For unnecessary roughness: Loss of 15 yards and an automatic first down. The player may be disqualified if the action is judged by the official(s) to be flagrant.
pro.note: The statement gives the first down with no offense or defense qualifier (B8.1.2 edge case).

college.absent: Section 1 has no separate foul for contact against a defenseless player; forcible contact to the head or neck of a defenseless player is targeting (9-1-4) and contact on a player out of the play is 9-1-12 (unnecessary roughness here).

entries.name: Impermissible use of the helmet

pro.q: Penalty: For impermissible use of the helmet: Loss of 15 yards. If the foul is by the defense, it is also an automatic first down. The player may be disqualified.

college.absent: No separate foul: forcible contact with the crown of the helmet is targeting (9-1-3), catalogued as targeting.

entries.name: Roughing the passer

pro.q: Penalty: For roughing the passer: Loss of 15 yards and an automatic first down; disqualification, if flagrant.

college.q: a. No defensive player shall unnecessarily rough a passer, when it is obvious the ball has been thrown.

entries.name: Roughing the kicker or holder

pro.q: (1) For roughing the kicker: Loss of 15 yards from the previous spot (personal foul) and an automatic first down. The player may be disqualified if the action is flagrant.

college.q: PENALTY—Roughing or any other personal foul against the kicker who is in the act or just after kicking the ball; or roughing the holder: 15 yards from the previous spot, plus automatic first down if not in conflict with other rules [S38 and S30].

entries.name: Running into the kicker or holder

pro.q: (2) For running into the kicker: Loss of five yards from the previous spot (not a personal foul). There is not an automatic first down.

college.q: Running into the kicker or holder: 5 yards from the previous spot [S30].

entries.name: Striking, kicking, kneeing or tripping

pro.q: Penalty: For prohibited acts in (a-e) above: Loss of 15 yards. If a foul is judged by the official(s) to be flagrant, the offender may be disqualified

college.q: No person subject to the rules shall strike an opponent with the knee

entries.name: Face mask

pro.q: Penalty: For twisting, turning, pushing, pulling, or controlling the mask or helmet opening: Loss of 15 yards. The player may be disqualified if the action is flagrant.

college.q: No player shall grasp and then twist, turn or pull the face mask, chin strap or any helmet opening of an opponent.

entries.name: Horse-collar tackle

pro.q: Penalty: For a horse-collar tackle: Loss of 15 yards and an automatic first down.

college.q: ARTICLE 15. All players are prohibited from grabbing the inside back or side collar of the shoulder pads or jersey

entries.name: Use of a helmet as a weapon

pro.q: Penalty: For illegal use of a helmet as a weapon: Loss of 15 yards and automatic disqualification.

college.absent: Read Rule 9 in full: no foul for using a removed helmet as a weapon; the act falls under striking (9-1-2) or fighting (9-5).

entries.name: Hip-drop tackle

pro.q: Penalty: For a hip-drop tackle: Loss of 15 yards and an automatic first down.

college.absent: Searched the whole text for "hip-drop" and "hip drop": no hit; Section 1 lists no such foul.

entries.name: Targeting

pro.absent: Searched the whole text for "targeting": no hit. Helmet contact is 12-2-10 (helmet_use) and hits on a defenseless player are 12-2-9 (defenseless_player).

college.q: ARTICLE 3. No player shall target and make forcible contact against an opponent with the crown of their helmet.
college.note: Articles 3 (crown of the helmet) and 4 (head or neck of a defenseless player) share one penalty.

entries.name: Unsportsmanlike conduct

pro.q: Penalty: For unsportsmanlike conduct (a) through (h): Loss of 15 yards from the succeeding spot or whatever spot the Referee, after consulting with the crew, deems equitable. If the foul is by the defense, it is also an automatic first down.

college.q: PENALTY—Unsportsmanlike conduct. Live-ball fouls by players: 15 yards [S27].

entries.name: Illegal bat

pro.q: Penalty: For illegal batting or kicking the ball: Loss of 10 yards. If the foul is by Team A before possession changes during a scrimmage down: Loss of down and loss of 10 yards
pro.note: Runoff: 4-7-1-f names batting or kicking the ball out of bounds only.

college.q: PENALTY—10 yards and loss of down for fouls by Team A if the loss of down is not in conflict with other rules [S31 and S9]

entries.name: Illegally kicking the ball

pro.q: Penalty: For illegal batting or kicking the ball: Loss of 10 yards. If the foul is by Team A before possession changes during a scrimmage down: Loss of down and loss of 10 yards
pro.note: Runoff: 4-7-1-f names batting or kicking the ball out of bounds only.

college.q: PENALTY—10 yards, plus loss of down for fouls by Team A if the loss of down is not in conflict with other rules

entries.name: Free kick offside or illegal free kick formation

pro.q: Penalty: For a player being beyond the restraining line when the ball is kicked (offside), a player being out of bounds when the ball is kicked, either team being in an illegal formation when the ball is kicked, kicking team players (other than the kicker) or receiving team players in the setup zone moving before permitted, or kicker moving beyond 15 yards from the kicker’s restraining line before permitted (illegal formation): Loss of five yards.

college.q: PENALTY [b-c5]—Live-ball foul. Five yards from the previous spot

entries.name: Illegal wedge on a free kick

pro.q: Penalty: For an illegal wedge block or an illegal double team block: Loss of 15 yards.
pro.note: During the kick it is enforced from the spot of the foul, during the return as customary; the spot field is false.

college.q: PENALTY—Noncontact foul. 15 yards, spot of the foul, or 15 yards, spot where the subsequent dead ball belongs to Team B

entries.name: Kick catch interference

pro.q: (a) For kick catch interference (interference with the opportunity to make a catch when a prior signal has not been made): Loss of 15 yards from the spot of the foul
pro.note: A kicking team foul: the receiving team takes the ball with a new series, so the automatic-first-down field is false.

college.q: Receiving team’s ball, first down, 15 yards beyond the spot of the foul for an interference foul [S33].
college.note: A kicking team foul: the receiving team takes the ball with a new series, so the automatic-first-down field is false.

entries.name: Contact with a player who has made a fair catch

pro.q: Penalty: For illegal contact with a player who has made a fair catch: Loss of 15 yards from the dead ball spot and disqualification if flagrant.
pro.note: A kicking team foul: the receiving team takes the ball with a new series, so the automatic-first-down field is false.

college.q: PENALTY—Dead-ball foul. Receiving team’s ball 15 yards from the succeeding spot [S7 and S38].
college.note: A kicking team foul: the receiving team takes the ball with a new series, so the automatic-first-down field is false.

entries.name: Invalid fair catch signal

pro.q: Penalty: For an invalid fair catch signal: Loss of five yards from the spot of the signal.

college.q: There is no illegal fair catch in the NCAA Football Rules.

entries.name: Illegal scrimmage kick (beyond the line)

pro.q: Penalty: For a punt, drop kick, or place kick that is kicked beyond the line of scrimmage or not from scrimmage: Loss of down and five yards from the spot of the kick.

college.q: PENALTY—For an illegal kick beyond the neutral zone (live-ball foul): Five yards from the previous spot and loss of down [S31 and S9].

entries.name: Ineligible player downfield before a scrimmage kick

pro.q: Penalty: For ineligible player downfield before the ball is kicked: Loss of five yards.

college.absent: The scrimmage kick section was read in full; it has no rule holding kicking team players at the line until the kick (see punt.release).

entries.name: Delay of game for spiking or throwing the ball after the down

pro.q: Penalty: For delay of the game: Loss of five yards: (a) from the succeeding spot if it occurs between downs and the ball remains dead; or

runoff_eligible.q: (e) spiking or throwing the ball in the field of play after a down has ended, except after a touchdown; or

dead_ball.q: (e) spiking or throwing the ball in the field of play after a down has ended, except after a score;

pro.note: Part (a) of the delay penalty: a spike after the down is a dead-ball foul enforced from the succeeding spot.

college.absent: Read the illegal delay list (3-4-2-b items 1 to 8) and searched the book for spiking: the only mention is the passer who spikes to stop the clock (7-3-2-f). A spike or throw after the down is not named as a delay foul.

entries.name: Excess team timeout after the two-minute warning

pro.q: Penalty: For the second and each subsequent excess team timeout after the two-minute warning: Loss of five yards from the succeeding spot for delay of the game.

runoff_eligible.q: (3) If an excess team timeout is charged against a team in possession of the ball, and the timeout causes the clock to stop or delays the clock from starting on the ready for play signal, the ball shall not be put in play until the time on the game clock has been reduced by 10 seconds

pro.note: The first excess timeout carries no yardage (Note 1); the value is the penalty for the second and later ones. An excess timeout is an exception to the automatic first down (14-1-2 Item 5 exception 6), so afd is false.

college.absent: Read 3-3-1-b: when a team asks for a timeout it does not have, the officials shall not acknowledge the request. The book names no excess-timeout foul or yardage.

entries.name: Illegal substitution (substitute enters during a live ball)

pro.q: (b) For a substitute entering the field during a live ball: Loss of five yards.

runoff_eligible.q: Penalty: For illegal substitution: Loss of five yards (unless a larger distance penalty is applicable) and a 10-second runoff.

pro.note: Live-ball case (5-2-8-b); the dead-ball 12-in-huddle case is too_many_in_formation. Illegal substitution is an exception to the automatic first down (14-1-2 Item 5 exception 5).

college.q: PENALTY [a-b] Live-ball foul. Five yards from the previous spot [S22].

entries.name: Second forward pass or pass after the ball returned behind the line

pro.q: (b) For a second forward pass from behind the line, or for a forward pass that was thrown after the ball returned behind the line: Loss of down and five yards from the previous spot.

college.q: PENALTY [a-e]—Five yards from the spot of the foul; also loss of down if by Team A before team possession changes during a scrimmage down (A.R. 3-4-3-IV and A.R. 7-3-2-II) [S35 and S9].

entries.name: Forward pass after a change of possession

pro.q: (c) For a forward pass that is thrown after a change of possession: Loss of five yards from where the ball is released.
pro.note: Enforced from where the ball is released, which is the spot of the foul; no loss of down.

college.q: PENALTY [a-e]—Five yards from the spot of the foul; also loss of down if by Team A before team possession changes during a scrimmage down (A.R. 3-4-3-IV and A.R. 7-3-2-II) [S35 and S9].

yards.q: c. It is thrown after team possession has changed during the down.

entries.name: Illegal cut block against an eligible receiver

class.q: ARTICLE 3. ILLEGAL CUT BLOCK. See Rule 8-4-5.

entries.name: Peel back block

pro.q: Penalty: For a peel back block: Loss of 15 yards.

entries.name: Illegal crackback block

pro.q: Penalty: For an illegal crackback block: Loss of 15 yards.

college.absent: Searched the 2026 NCAA text for crackback and read Rule 9 Section 1: there is no crackback block foul. The nearest rule is the blind-side block (9-1-18).

entries.name: Roughing the holder

pro.q: Penalty: For roughing the holder: Loss of 15 yards from the previous spot (personal foul) and an automatic first down. The player may be disqualified if the action is flagrant.

college.q: PENALTY—Roughing or any other personal foul against the kicker who is in the act or just after kicking the ball; or roughing the holder: 15 yards from the previous spot, plus automatic first down if not in conflict with other rules [S38 and S30].

entries.name: Taunting (baiting or taunting acts or words)

If the foul is by the defense, it is also an automatic first down. If the action is flagrant and a game official sees the entire action, the player is also disqualified.

If the infraction is flagrant, the player is also disqualified. If the foul is by the defense, it is also an automatic first down.

college.q: PENALTY [a-d]—15 yards, previous spot and automatic first down. [S38]

yards.q: 2. Place a hand(s) on a teammate to get leverage for additional height.

entries.name: Leaping to block a field goal or try

pro.q: Penalty: For unsportsmanlike conduct (i) through (v): Loss of 15 yards from: (a) the succeeding spot if the ball is dead; or (b) the previous spot if the ball was in play. If the infraction is flagrant, the player is also disqualified. If the foul is by the defense, it is also an automatic first down.

yards.q: (r) Running forward and leaping across the line of scrimmage in an obvious attempt to block a field goal or Try Kick, or apparent kick, unless the leaping player was in a stationary position within one yard of the line of scrimmage when the ball was snapped.

college.q: PENALTY [a-d]—15 yards, previous spot and automatic first down. [S38]

yards.q: b. It is a foul if a defensive player moves forward and tries to block a kick or apparent kick on a field goal or try by leaving their feet and leaping into the plane directly above the frame of the body of an opponent.

entries.name: Multiple fouls to manipulate the game clock

pro.q: Penalty: For multiple fouls to run off time from the game clock: Loss of 15 yards, and the game clock will be reset to where it was at the snap. After the penalty is enforced, the game clock will start on the next snap.
pro.note: The clock reset is applied by the clock module; this row holds the yardage.

college.absent: Read 3-4-3 (unfair clock tactics): the referee orders the clock started or stopped, with no yardage penalty. Repeated fouls that halve the distance are an unfair act (9-2-3-b), covered by palpably_unfair.

entries.name: Palpably unfair act (referee equitable penalty)

pro.q: Penalty: For a palpably unfair act: Offender may be disqualified. The Referee, after consulting the officiating crew, enforces any such distance penalty as they consider equitable and irrespective of any other specified code penalty.
pro.note: No fixed distance: the Referee sets it (yards 0, enforcement equitable). The rule says the offender may be disqualified, stored as if_flagrant.

college.q: PENALTY—Unsportsmanlike conduct. The referee may take any action they consider equitable, which includes directing that the down be repeated, including assessing a 15-yard penalty, awarding a score, or suspending or forfeiting the game [S27].
college.note: No fixed distance: the referee acts equitably (yards 0).

entries.name: League-office disqualification for a flagrant act

pro.q: Penalty: Loss of 15 yards and disqualification from the game if actions are found to be flagrant.

college.absent: Read 9-6 (flagrant personal fouls): a conference may review a game after it is played and suspend a player, but no rule lets an off-field office disqualify a player during the game. Targeting is reviewed by the replay official (Rule 12), not a league office.

entries.name: Unsportsmanlike conduct by a non-player

pro.q: Penalty: For unsportsmanlike conduct: Loss of 15 yards. Enforcement is from: (a) the succeeding spot if the ball is dead; (b) the previous spot if the ball was in play; or (c) whatever spot the Referee, after consulting with the crew, deems equitable. (palpably unfair act).

dq.q: Violations before or during the game may also result in disqualification.

pro.note: The Referee may also exclude a flagrant offender (13-1-6).

college.q: PENALTY [1-4]—Unsportsmanlike conduct. Dead-ball foul. 15 yards from the succeeding spot [S7 and S27]. Automatic first down for fouls by Team B if not in conflict with other rules. Flagrant offenders, if players or substitutes, shall be ejected [S47].

entries.name: Unnecessary physical contact with a game official

pro.q: Penalty: For unsportsmanlike conduct (a) through (h): Loss of 15 yards from the succeeding spot or whatever spot the Referee, after consulting with the crew, deems equitable. If the foul is by the defense, it is also an automatic first down. If the action is flagrant and a game official sees the entire action, the player is also disqualified.

dq.q: The player shall be disqualified from the game, and any such action must be reported to the Commissioner, who may impose further discipline.

pro.note: Always a foul between downs (14-1-2 Item 4 exception), carried by foul.foul_against_official.separate; dead_ball stays false.

college.q: PENALTY—Unsportsmanlike conduct. Administer as a dead-ball foul. 15 yards from the succeeding spot and automatic ejection. Automatic first down for fouls by Team B if not in conflict with other rules. [S7, S27 and S47].

entries.name: Challenge with no timeout left

pro.q: Penalty: For initiating a challenge when a team has exhausted its timeouts: Loss of 15 yards enforced as a foul between downs.
pro.note: Always a foul between downs (14-1-2 Item 4 exception), carried by foul.challenge_without_timeout.separate.

college.absent: Read 12-5-1-b-6: a head coach may not challenge when team timeouts are not available or are exhausted; 3-3-1-b says the officials do not acknowledge such a request. No penalty is named.

entries.name: Fifth and later excess timeout for injury

pro.q: Penalty: For the second and each subsequent excess team timeout after the two-minute warning: Loss of five yards from the succeeding spot for delay of the game.

yards.q: (A penalty for a fifth and subsequent excess timeout for injury shall be considered a foul between downs

college.absent: Read Appendix G and 3-3-6: an injured player the officials stop for is a charged timeout or a referee timeout; the book has no excess-timeout foul for injury.

entries.name: Free kick: kicking team player not set on the line

pro.q: Penalty: For a player being beyond the restraining line when the ball is kicked (offside), a player being out of bounds when the ball is kicked, or either team being in an illegal formation when the ball is kicked: Loss of 5 yards.

yards.q: (1) All kicking team players other than the kicker and the holder must be lined up with their front foot on the kicking team’s restraining line, and both feet must remain on the ground until the ball is kicked; and

pro.note: Onside-kick alignment rule; the penalty is the shared free-kick formation penalty.

college.absent: Read 6-1-2 (free kick formation): a Team A player not behind the ball when it is kicked is the formation foul already held by free_kick_offside; the book has no separate early-movement foul.

entries.name: Illegal free kick

pro.q: Penalty: For illegal free kick: Loss of five yards.

college.q: PENALTY—Dead ball foul. Illegal kick. Five yards from the succeeding spot [S7 and S19]. (A.R. 6-1-2-I).

entries.name: Illegal blocking or use of hands on a free kick

pro.q: Penalty: For illegal blocking or use of hands by either team: Loss of 10 yards.

college.q: PENALTY —Live-ball foul. Five yards from the previous spot, or five yards from the spot where the subsequent dead ball belongs to Team B, or from the spot where the ball is placed after a touchback [S19].

entries.name: Illegal double team block on a free kick

pro.q: Penalty: For an illegal wedge block or an illegal double team block: Loss of 15 yards. If the foul occurs during the kick, enforcement is from the spot of the foul.

yards.q: (c) A “double team block” is permissible only by players who were initially lined up in the setup zone at the time of the kick.

pro.note: During the kick it is enforced from the spot of the foul, during the return as customary; the spot field is false (same reading as illegal_wedge).

college.absent: Read 6-1-10 (illegal wedge formation) and searched the book for double team: the only hit is an officiating note on holding. No double-team foul on a free kick.

entries.name: Onside kick untouched beyond the setup zone

pro.q: Penalty: For an onside kick that goes untouched beyond the onside kick setup zone: Unsportsmanlike conduct: Loss of 15 yards from the kicking team’s restraining line and the receiving team takes possession.

college.absent: Read Rule 6 Section 1 (free kicks). The 2026 NCAA book has no onside-kick declaration or setup-zone rule, so no such foul.

entries.name: Illegal touching of a free kick by the kicking team

pro.q: Penalty: For illegal touching of an onside kick by the kicking team: Loss of five yards, or the receiving team takes possession of the ball at the spot of the illegal touch.
pro.note: Item 2 (out of bounds first) has the same 5 yards without the option.

college.q: Any other touching by Team A is illegal touching, a violation that, when the ball becomes dead, gives the receiving team the privilege of taking the ball at the spot of the violation.
college.note: A violation, not a distance penalty: yards 0; the receiving team may take the ball at the spot.

entries.name: Kicking team player out of bounds on a free kick

pro.q: Penalty: For voluntarily going out of bounds on a free kick without contact: Loss of five yards.

college.q: PENALTY—Live-ball foul. Five yards from the previous spot, or five yards from the spot where the subsequent dead ball belongs to Team B, or from the spot where the ball is placed after a touchback [S19]
college.note: College fouls the player who goes out and returns inbounds (6-1-11), the nearest rule.

entries.name: Running into the free kicker

pro.q: Penalty: For running into the kicker: Loss of five yards.

college.absent: Read 9-1-16: running into the kicker is written for scrimmage kicks; for a free kick 6-1-9 bars blocking the kicker for five yards (15 yards, a different foul). No free-kick running-into foul.

entries.name: Kicking team player voluntarily out of bounds on a scrimmage kick

pro.q: Penalty: For a kicking team player voluntarily going out of bounds on a scrimmage kick: Loss of five yards.

college.q: PENALTY—Live-ball foul. Five yards from the previous spot or if the scrimmage kick crosses the neutral zone, five yards from the spot where the subsequent dead ball belongs to Team B [S19].
college.note: College fouls the player who goes out and returns inbounds, the nearest rule.

entries.name: Defensive illegal formation against a scrimmage kick

pro.q: Penalty: For illegal formation by the defense: Loss of five yards.
pro.note: Exception (10) to the automatic first down: illegal formation by the defense during a scrimmage kick play.

college.q: it is illegal for three Team B players on their line of scrimmage inside the blocking zone to align shoulder-to-shoulder and move forward together after the snap with primary contact against a single Team A player (A.R. 6-3-14-III and IV). PENALTY—Live-ball foul. Five yards, previous spot. [S19]

entries.name: Pushing teammates into the offensive formation

pro.q: Penalty: For pushing teammates into offensive formation: Loss of 15 yards.

college.absent: Searched the 2026 NCAA text for pushing teammates into a formation: the only hit is 9-1-11-d-3 (a player pushed or propelled to block a kick), which is kick_block_leverage.

entries.name: Pull-and-shoot holding to block a kick

pro.q: Penalty: For defensive holding: Loss of five yards and an automatic first down.

yards.q: (b) during a punt, field goal attempt, or Try kick attempt, B1 grabs and pulls an offensive player out of the way, allowing B2 to shoot the gap (pull-and-shoot) in an attempt to block an apparent kick, except if B1 is advancing toward the kicker.

college.q: PENALTY [c-e]—10 yards plus automatic first down if the first down is not in conflict with other rules [S42].
college.note: College has no separate pull-and-shoot foul; the block attempt is defensive holding under 9-3-4-d.

entries.name: Holding or illegal hands during a scrimmage kick (not a block attempt)

pro.q: (e) During a scrimmage kick play that goes beyond the line of scrimmage, the penalty yardage for holding and illegal use of hands fouls by either team shall be 10 yards unless the foul is committed in an attempt to block the kick (see 14-4-8).
pro.note: A receiving team (Team B) foul gains the first down by the general rule.

college.q: PENALTY—10 yards Penalties for Team A fouls behind the neutral zone are enforced from the previous spot. Safety if the foul occurs behind Team A’s goal line [S42].

afd.q: PENALTY [c-e]—10 yards plus automatic first down if the first down is not in conflict with other rules [S42].

entries.name: Illegal touching of a scrimmage kick after going out of bounds

pro.q: Penalty: For illegal touching of a scrimmage kick: Loss of five yards. If the illegal touching is inside the receiver’s five- yard line, in addition to the other specified options, the receiving team may elect to take a touchback.

college.q: This is illegal touching, a violation that, when the ball becomes dead, gives the receiving team the privilege of taking the ball at the spot of the violation
college.note: A violation, not a distance penalty: yards 0. College has no rule keyed to a player who went out of bounds.

entries.name: Interference with a fair catch after a signal

pro.q: (b) For fair catch interference (interfering with a fair catch after a signal): Loss of 15 yards from the spot of the foul. A fair catch is awarded even if the ball is not caught.
pro.note: A kicking team foul: the receiving team takes the ball with a new series, so the automatic-first-down field is false.

college.q: Receiving team’s ball, first down, 15 yards beyond the spot of the foul for an interference foul [S33].
college.note: College has one interference foul for both cases; same row as kick_catch_interference. A kicking team foul, so afd is false.

entries.name: Interference with the opportunity to catch a muffed kick

pro.q: Penalty: For interference with the opportunity to make a fair catch after a muff: A fair catch is awarded at the spot of the interference even if the ball is not caught.
pro.note: No distance: a fair catch is awarded. 15 more yards only if it is unnecessary roughness.

college.q: b. If a Team B player makes a valid fair catch signal, the unimpeded opportunity to catch a free or scrimmage kick continues if this player muffs the kick and still has an opportunity to complete the catch.

yards.q: Receiving team’s ball, first down, 15 yards beyond the spot of the foul for an interference foul [S33].

college.note: College applies the 6-4-1 interference penalty to a muff after a signal.

entries.name: Illegal block after a fair catch signal

pro.q: Penalty: For an illegal block after a fair catch signal: Loss of 15 yards from the spot of the foul.
pro.note: Committed by the receiving team; the signaller is the offender.

college.q: PENALTY—Free kick: Receiving team’s ball 10 yards from the spot of the foul [S40]. Scrimmage kick: 10 yards, postscrimmage kick enforcement [S40]. If a Personal Foul is committed in conjunction with this action, the penalty is 15 yards and flagrant offenders shall be ejected or disqualified.
college.note: College block by the fair catch signaller is 10 yards; 15 only if a personal foul.
